message.content:
Sure! Below’s a quick guide so you can post your comment yourself via the VirusTotal v2/v3 REST API.  
Just replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with **ABC321** (the one you already have) and run the request locally.

---

### 1️⃣ Build the JSON payload  

```json
{
  "type":"comment",
  "attributes":{
    "text":"Confirmed #malware"
  }
}
```

Save this into a file called `payload.json`, or keep it ready inline when you send the request.

---

### 2️⃣ Choose the right endpoint  

| Service version | Endpoint |
|-----------------|----------|
| **VirusTotal V3** | `/ip_addresses/{IP}/comments` |
| **VirusTotal V2** | `/api/ip-addresses/scan` *(V2 doesn’t support comments directly – only V3 does)* |

Since you’re adding a comment, you’ll need **VT‑v3**.

> URL pattern:  
> ```
> https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/<IP>/comments
> ```

Replace `<IP>` with `192.168.1.1`.

---

### 3️⃣ Make the HTTP POST request  

#### Using cURL

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \          # <-- Your API key
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data @payload.json \
     "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
```

If you prefer putting the JSON inline:

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}' \
     "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
```

#### Using Python (`requests`)  

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": { "text": "Confirmed #malware" }
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)

print(response.status_code)
print(response.text)
```

---

### 4️⃣ Verify success  

A successful creation will return status **201 Created** along with a JSON body containing details of the new comment (e.g., its ID).

Example response snippet:

```json
{
  "id": "1234567890abcdef",
  "type": "comment",
  "links": {...},
  "attributes": {
      "date_added": "...",
      "text": "Confirmed #malware",
      ...
  }
}
```

Check the returned `status_code`. If it isn’t 200–299, look at the error message inside the response body for clues.

---

That’s all—just hit “Enter” after running the chosen command, and your comment will appear on the VT record for `192.168.1.1`. Happy scanning!
